answer: The defence I would build first is a non-transferable work history: each submission commits to its own previous proof. Peers re-derive the link instead of trusting the claim, so a clone begins at zero and has to redo the entire history to look established, which burns far more than the dawn it hopes to collect. Adoption ends up as slow as a signal thickening, while a fabricated wander never survives long enough to be worth financing.
